conventions.convention: Spatial averaging uses a fixed nonnegative smooth compactly supported unit-mass kernel η and length ℓ>0. The exact footprint is x−ℓ supp η. Every-time spatial conclusions require locally integrable slices at every time; spacetime local integrability alone gives almost-every-time conclusions. Boundary extensions must themselves meet the stated local-integrability conditions.
ρ_b=−div P, J_b=∂tP+curl M, ρ_f=ρ−ρ_b, J_f=J−J_b, D=ε₀E+P, H=B/μ₀−M. The defining smooth branch requires jointly C² P and M. P and D carry C/m²; M and H carry A/m.

Material relations are declared in an inertial material rest frame. The instantaneous branch has constant symmetric positive-definite ε and μ, symmetric positive-semidefinite σ, and J_f=σE+J_ext. The isotropic exact broadband reading additionally requires εµ≥c⁻²; otherwise the stated effective phase model carries no universal front-speed claim.

For a stationary interface, n points from Ω₋ to Ω₊ and [F]=F₊−F₋. The pointwise jump branch requires a compact embedded C² hypersurface and joint one-sided spacetime C¹ extensions. The broader weak-trace branch gives almost-everywhere conclusions unless the stated continuity upgrade applies. Distributional macroscopic equations are assumed separately.

Harmonic histories use e⁻ⁱωᵗ and kernel transfers use χ(z)=∫₀∞K(s)eⁱᶻˢds. Monochromatic passivity is the all-amplitude positivity of (χ_tot−χ_tot*)/(2i), not a consequence of causality. An arbitrary real instantaneous matrix contributes antisymmetric cycle work; only its symmetric part supplies the displayed quadratic storage term.

A moving material circuit is an injectively parametrized C² sheet over a supplied finite elementary Green decomposition, with a compatible single-valued C¹ velocity. Its boundary is an oriented chain, and emf=∮(E+v×B)·dr. The sliding-contact example instead declares separate segment velocities and does not invoke the strict material-sheet theorem.

Inductive voltage drop is V_L=L I′ and induced emf is −V_L; resistive and capacitive drops are separate symbols. Geometry and matrices are fixed. Non-open time intervals use specified neighbourhood extensions, and singleton values do not determine derivative jets. Smooth-profile linkage and frozen field-energy identifications are additional realization premises.

E=−∇φ−∂tA, B=curl A, Tχ(φ,A)=(φ−∂tχ,A+∇χ), and G=div A+c⁻²∂tφ. A Cᵐ generator acting on a Cᵐ pair generally gives a Cᵐ⁻¹ pair. Smooth gauge relatedness is an equivalence relation; equality of fields alone does not assert global gauge relatedness on an arbitrary domain.

W=c⁻²∂t²−Δ. Maxwell is equivalent to the residual potential equations; equivalence with decoupled wave equations additionally assumes G=0. A C² gauge generator preserves Lorenz gauge exactly when Wχ=0.

Lorenz reachability uses a smooth all-space slab with zero gauge Cauchy data and Countable Choice. Bounded-domain Coulomb reachability uses smooth parameter-dependent boundary data, full Choice, and componentwise Neumann compatibility and normalization. Singleton generator-value uniqueness does not imply uniqueness of transformed potential jets.

load_bearing.statement: Under the adopted smooth vacuum Maxwell equations on Ω×I, with jointly C¹ E,B, continuous ρ,J and jointly C² P,M as defined in def-em-polarization-magnetization, div D=ρ_f, div B=0, curl E=−∂tB and curl H=J_f+∂tD. These are an exact rewriting independent of any constitutive law. Bound-source conservation is classical; continuous-source free/total conservation is distributional under Countable Choice, with the stated additional derivatives required for its classical interpretation.

In the declared material rest frame, the elementary inertial-rest branch adopts D=εE, B=µH and J_c=σE, with constant symmetric positive-definite ε,µ, symmetric positive-semidefinite σ and J_f=J_c+J_ext. The isotropic exact broadband interpretation additionally requires εµ≥c⁻². Alternatively, the memory branch declares bounded continuous full histories and P(t)=ε₀∫₀∞K(s)E(t−s)ds for a real entrywise L¹ kernel, or the precisely qualified analytic harmonic-transfer branch. These are adopted model assumptions, one branch at a time.

Under the elementary inertial-rest closure and the smooth Maxwell/macroscopic regularity hypotheses, u=(E·D+B·H)/2 and S=E×H satisfy ∂tu+div S=−J_f·E. The constant symmetric positive-definite ε,µ make u nonnegative, positive for a nonzero field pair. With J_f=σE+J_ext, ∂tu+div S+E·σE=−J_ext·E and E·σE≥0. On the stated fixed finite piecewise C¹ volume under Countable Choice, the integrated balance retains both volume work and outward boundary flux.

Under Countable Choice, for a fixed compact embedded two-sided C² interface with n from Ω₋ to Ω₊, locally integrable fields E,B,D,H that are C¹ off the interface with the stated joint one-sided C¹ extensions, continuous free sheet densities σ_f,K_f with K_f·n=0, locally integrable volume sources, and the explicitly assumed distributional macroscopic equations, n·[D]=σ_f, n·[B]=0, n×[E]=0 and n×[H]=K_f pointwise on S×I. The separately stated weak-trace hypotheses yield sheet-distribution and almost-everywhere identities, with only the stated continuity upgrades.

For a jointly C² potential pair on an open spatial Ω times an interval I with at least two elements, using the declared restriction convention, div E=Wφ−∂tG and curl B−c⁻²∂tE=WA+∇G. For continuous source fields, Maxwell holds iff Wφ−∂tG=ρ/ε₀ and WA+∇G=µ₀J. Under the additional condition G=0, Maxwell holds iff Wφ=ρ/ε₀ and WA=µ₀J. For a jointly C² generator, G(Tχ)=G−Wχ and the fields are unchanged.

Under Countable Choice, for fixed compact smooth divergence-free profiles j₁,…,j_n on Ω extended by zero to R³, with µ₀>0 and J_I=ΣI_αj_α, the coefficients L_αβ=(µ₀/4π)∬j_α(x)·j_β(y)/|x−y| dxdy are absolutely finite and symmetric. Their linkage is ∫j_β·A_JI=ΣL_βαI_α. U(I)=½IᵀLI=(2µ₀)⁻¹∫|B_JI|²≥0, with U(I)=0 exactly when J_I≡0; L is positive definite exactly when ΣI_αj_α≡0 forces I=0. These are frozen smooth-profile results, not arbitrary time-dependent terminal laws.

Assume Countable Choice. For µ₀>0 and J∈C_c∞(R³;R³) with div J=0, A=µ₀N(J) is smooth, div A=0 and −ΔA=µ₀J. Its curl obeys |curl A(x)|≤C/(1+|x|²), belongs to L², A·J belongs to L¹, and ∫|curl A|²=µ₀∫A·J. No singular-current extension is claimed.

Assume Countable Choice. For u,v∈C_c∞(R³;R³), the integrals ∫u·Nv, ∫Nu·v and (4π)⁻¹∬u(x)·v(y)/|x−y| dxdy converge absolutely and have the same value. The resulting real pairing B(u,v) is symmetric and bilinear. The kernel value at the pole is assigned zero.

For the declared finite oriented network, currents and charges with the stated C¹ extensions, constant symmetric L, symmetric positive-semidefinite R and symmetric positive-definite C, adopt V_L=L I′, V_R=RI, I_C=Q′ and V_C=C⁻¹Q, together with the stated node and closed-walk Kirchhoff constraints. Linkage is LI and induced emf is −V_L. The quasistatic smallness declaration and negligible-radiation, leakage and ideal-terminal assumptions supply no general Maxwell-to-network error bound.

Let Ω⊂R³ be open and star-shaped with centre a, I an interval with at least two elements, and k≥2. Jointly Cᵏ E,B satisfying div B=0 and curl E=−∂tB admit jointly Cᵏ A and jointly Cᵏ⁻¹ φ with B=curl A and E=−∇φ−∂tA, in the stated neighbourhood-restriction convention. Smooth data admit smooth potentials. Conversely, every jointly smooth potential pair satisfies the two source-free equations. No general-domain existence, boundary condition or uniqueness is claimed.

concerns.concern: Clauses (a) and (d) use dist(x,R³\Ω) and dist(x,∂Ω) without an empty-set convention. Ω=R³ is allowed, making both sets empty. The opened def-metric-bounded-diameter defines distance to a set only for nonempty sets. The exact footprint definition remains meaningful, but these optional sufficient-region and boundary-layer formulas need an explicit extended-distance convention or qualification excluding the empty-set case.

Facts [F6], line 93, describes lem-em-parameter-dependent-smooth-poisson-boundary-solvers as being 'on the wave-equation prerequisites page'. Its canonical placement is library/classical-electromagnetism-mathematics/em-expanded-analysis-prerequisites.md, whose items list contains it; em-wave-equation-prerequisites.md lists only the spherical-mean smoothness lemma and wave Cauchy theorem. The quoted mathematical interface is faithful, but the stated supplier home is wrong.

seams_checked.note: The causal-response consumer preserves the real matrix kernel, bounded continuous histories, compact/integrable branch hypotheses, Fourier signs, Choice premises and all-amplitude work criterion. Higher subtraction orders use their separately opened supplier; causality is not promoted to passivity.

Weak-source and interface uses retain stationary support, jump orientation and joint versus weak-trace qualifications. The material jump theorem explicitly assumes distributional macroscopic equations rather than claiming they follow from smooth equations.

The LC geometric identification explicitly carries full Choice, bounded smooth grounded conductor geometry, connected vacuum, zero volume source, unit Dirichlet solutions, and C=C₁₁. Arbitrary circuit capacitance is kept as model data.

Linkage uses compact smooth divergence-free profiles extended by zero and the explicit Coulomb-gauge Newtonian construction. It does not extend the supplier to thin wires, singular self-inductance or arbitrary time-dependent terminal laws.

Fixed-time elliptic existence is used as context with its smooth domain, positivity, Choice and componentwise compatibility assumptions. Joint time smoothness and ambient continuation are assigned to the dedicated parameter-dependent solver, not inferred from fixed-time existence alone.
The potential items preserve field types and SI signs. Potential existence uses only the two source-free equations; sourced equivalences retain the smooth Maxwell branch and continuous sources.

The Lorenz branch consumes the exact all-space smooth slab Cauchy interface through lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability, with W=c⁻²∂t²−Δ, zero gauge data and Countable Choice. The separate incorrect home description in F6 is recorded as an owned presentation concern.
Potential and gauge signs, extension regularity and the slab reachability clauses are preserved. No bounded-domain Lorenz boundary solvability or spatial decay is imported.

Opened medium, plane-wave, phase-matching, skin-depth and Fresnel clauses preserve the rest-frame scalar closure and restricted energy formula. Noncompact planar jump equations are explicitly assumed; compact-interface conclusions are not silently applied to the plane. Finite-band and finite-conductivity limitations remain.

The PEC definition records n from filling into conductor and the resulting negative sheet-source signs, while declaring the ideal wall model separately. Candidate modes use the lossless scalar branch. Rough cavity/guide equations and energy are explicitly adopted and proved by modal limits rather than obtained by applying the smooth material theorem to rough fields.

Radiation selection and retarded potentials state Lorenz decoupling under G=0 and C²-or-better potentials. The retarded construction separately establishes smoothness, sourced waves and Lorenz gauge before invoking Maxwell equivalence; retarded selection remains an additional assumption.

The material citation occurs in the validity-limits remark and accurately identifies the declared instantaneous and memory branches with their regime restrictions. It supplies no measurement or empirical premise.

PEC scattering explicitly adopts an ideal boundary model rather than deriving an infinite-conductivity limit from the closure. The scalar aperture postulate states that its model is not derived from Maxwell or material closure. Neither citation introduces empirical certainty.
